skills.name: mobile-app-autopilot-getting-started
skills.description: Use for the Mobile App Autopilot bot's first conversation with a new owner, or when that owner says "set me up" or "start over" for their app.
skills.content:
---
name: mobile-app-autopilot-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the Mobile App Autopilot bot's first conversation with a new owner, or
  when that owner says "set me up" or "start over" for their app.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line, then ask setup questions ONE AT A TIME. Wait for each answer. Accept "skip" and move on.

Opening line (adapt tone, keep it short):
"I build and ship your iOS and Android app with you: spec, code (via cloud coding agents), store builds, listings, releases, and a weekly health check on crashes and reviews. A few quick questions first."

## Questions (in order, one per message)
1. "What are you building? Give me a sentence, or tell me you already have a repo and where it lives (GitHub, GitLab, other)."
2. "Any stack preference? My default is Expo + React Native + TypeScript (one codebase, both stores). I only go native Swift/Kotlin if you need it."
3. "Which of these accounts do you already have: Apple Developer Program, Google Play Console (personal or organization?), Expo? None is fine, I'll walk you through it when we need them."
4. "Want to connect any tools? GitHub (needed for an existing repo), Sentry or Firebase Crashlytics (crashes), Linear or Notion (tasks/docs). You can add them from the plugins/connectors page; I'll wait."
5. "What should I call you?"
6. "How often do you want an app health digest? Default is Monday 9am your time. Weekly, daily, or off?"

## After the answers
1. Save memories (short, factual): app one-liner, repo location or "new repo", stack, accounts held and account type (Play personal accounts created after Nov 13 2023 need the 12-tester closed test, see app-store-submission), connectors connected, owner's preferred name, digest cadence.
2. Create a routine named `weekly-app-health` on the chosen cron (default `0 9 * * 1`, daily `0 9 * * *`, skip if "off"), in the owner's timezone; confirm the time. Prompt:
   "Run the weekly-app-health skill for my app: crashes, ratings and reviews, open PRs and CI, build and rollout status, upcoming deadlines (Play target API, Apple minimum SDK, Expo SDK age, certificate and membership expiry), checking live official sources for version-sensitive rules. Send one digest of at most ~15 lines ending with the top 3 actions, compare with last week's saved summary, save this week's summary to memory. Do not open issues, post replies, launch paid builds, or start fixes without my OK; offer them instead."
   Optional: if GitHub is connected and the owner wants it, also create `pr-opened-review` (event: GitHub pull request opened on the app repo). Prompt:
   "A PR was opened on my app repo. Review it with the build-feature-with-cloud-agent step 3 checklist and say if it needs a new binary or can ship as an OTA update (release-train). If it came from your cloud agent and has problems, reply to that agent with numbered fixes; otherwise send me a 5-line summary with a merge recommendation. Do not merge or comment publicly unless I said so."
3. Pick the next step and say it in one line:
   - Idea only: run `app-idea-to-spec`.
   - Spec ready or simple idea: run `scaffold-mobile-app`.
   - Existing repo: ask the owner to confirm the repo, then launch a read-only cloud agent to audit it (Expo SDK version, targetSdk, eas.json, tests, CI, Sentry) and report gaps. Feed gaps into `build-feature-with-cloud-agent`.
4. Missing accounts: explain cost and lead time once. Apple Developer Program is a paid annual membership; Google Play has a one-time registration fee; check current prices on the official sites, never from memory. Identity verification can take days, so start early. The owner signs up and signs in themselves.

## Rules to state once, early
- I never submit to the stores, buy anything, or message anyone without your explicit yes.
- I never ask for passwords. Sign-ins happen on your side; keys go into Expo/EAS or bot secrets, not chat.
- Code changes go through cloud agents as branches/PRs you can review.

Keep onboarding under ~8 messages; answer questions as they come.

skills.name: app-idea-to-spec
skills.description: Use when the owner has a rough app idea (or a vague feature list) and needs a one-page product spec before any code is written.
skills.content:
---
name: app-idea-to-spec
description: >-
  Use when the owner has a rough app idea (or a vague feature list) and needs a
  one-page product spec before any code is written.
---
# App idea to one-page spec

Goal: a spec a cloud agent can build from, in one sitting. Ask at most 3-4 questions, only those whose answers change the architecture or the MVP. Make sensible defaults for the rest and label them "assumed".

## Questions worth asking (pick the ones still unknown)
- Who is the user and what single job does the app do for them, in one sentence?
- Do users need accounts, and do they share data with other users (social, teams) or only with themselves?
- Must it work offline? (changes data layer)
- How will it make money: free, paid upfront, subscription, one-time unlock, ads? (changes store setup, see `monetization-setup`)
- Any hard device features: camera, location in background, push, Bluetooth, HealthKit/Health Connect, payments for physical goods?

## Quick market check (5 minutes, cite links)
Search both stores and the web for 3-5 comparable apps. Note what they charge, their common 1-2 star complaints, and the gap. Never invent download or revenue numbers; if unknown, say unknown. Warn if the idea is a thin clone or a website wrapper (App Review 4.2 Minimum Functionality, 4.3 Spam).

## Spec template (write to docs/SPEC.md in the repo, or a file on the box if no repo yet)
```
# <App name (working)> - Spec v1
One-liner:
Target user:
Core loop: (trigger -> action -> reward -> return reason)
Screens (MVP): 1. Onboarding 2. ... (each: purpose, key components, empty/error states)
Navigation: tabs/stack outline (expo-router file routes)
Data model: entities, fields, relations; local vs server
Auth: none | anonymous | email/OTP | Sign in with Apple + Google (4.8 requires an equivalent privacy-focused option, e.g. Sign in with Apple, if any third-party social login is offered)
Backend: none | Supabase | Firebase | existing API (assumed/decided)
Offline: none | read cache | full offline sync
Permissions + why (becomes iOS purpose strings and Data safety answers)
Monetization: model, products, free vs paid line
Analytics + crash reporting: Sentry or Crashlytics
MVP cut: IN (must ship) / LATER (explicitly deferred)
Account deletion: in-app path + web URL (required by both stores if accounts exist)
Risks: review risks, technical risks, legal (health, finance, kids, UGC moderation)
Open questions:
```

## Rules
- MVP = smallest set that delivers the core loop end to end. Push everything else to LATER.
- UGC apps need report/block/filter and moderation (App Review 1.2); kids apps need the Kids category rules; health/finance claims need care. Flag these in Risks.
- Show the spec, ask "Build this MVP?" On yes, go to `scaffold-mobile-app`, passing the spec file path.

skills.name: scaffold-mobile-app
skills.description: Use when starting a new mobile app codebase (or re-platforming one) from a spec, before feature work begins.
skills.content:
---
name: scaffold-mobile-app
description: >-
  Use when starting a new mobile app codebase (or re-platforming one) from a
  spec, before feature work begins.
---
# Scaffold a mobile app

## 1. Choose the stack
Default: Expo (latest stable SDK) + React Native + TypeScript + expo-router, EAS Build/Submit/Update, development builds (not Expo Go) for real testing.
Check the current SDK at runtime: fetch https://expo.dev/changelog and https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/. Reference point (Oct 2026): SDK 57 stable (React Native 0.86, React 19.2, released June 30 2026; use expo@57.0.17+ for Hermes fixes), SDK 58 in beta since Sep 15 2026. Never scaffold on a beta unless the owner asks.
Go native (SwiftUI + Kotlin/Compose, two repos or a monorepo) only if the owner needs it: heavy platform APIs, watch/widgets-first, existing native team. Explain the cost: two codebases, iOS builds need Xcode Cloud or a Mac runner since this computer is Linux.

## 2. Pick the repo
- New app: launch the cloud agent with new_repo (private Cursor Origin repo), or the owner's empty GitHub repo if they prefer.
- Existing repo: confirm owner, name, default branch.

## 3. Cloud agent prompt (fill the <> parts, keep it precise)
```
Scaffold a production-ready Expo app in this repo.
- Use `npx create-expo-app@latest` (TypeScript, expo-router). Remove demo screens.
- App name "<Name>", slug "<slug>", scheme "<scheme>".
- app.config.ts: ios.bundleIdentifier "<com.company.app>", android.package "<com.company.app>", ios.supportsTablet <false unless iPad is in scope>, version "1.0.0", runtimeVersion { policy: "fingerprint" }, updates url placeholder via EAS.
- Routes for these MVP screens: <list from SPEC>. Typed routes on.
- Env: expo public vars via EXPO_PUBLIC_*, secrets only via EAS environment variables; add .env.example; never commit secrets.
- Quality: ESLint (expo config) + Prettier, `tsc --noEmit`, Jest + @testing-library/react-native with one smoke test per screen. npm scripts: lint, typecheck, test.
- eas.json: cli.appVersionSource "remote"; profiles development (developmentClient, internal distribution), preview (internal, channel "preview"), production (autoIncrement true, channel "production").
- Install expo-dev-client, expo-updates, @sentry/react-native with its Expo config plugin (DSN from env).
- CI: GitHub Actions (or the host's CI) running lint, typecheck, test on PRs.
- Docs: README with setup, scripts, env vars, build commands. Keep docs/SPEC.md.
- Do not run eas build or eas submit. Do not add paid services.
Acceptance: `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test` pass; `npx expo-doctor` clean; app boots to the first screen.
```

## 4. Verify before reporting
- Read the PR diff: identifiers correct, no secrets, no leftover template screens, tests real (not empty).
- Check CI status on the PR. If red, reply to the agent with the failing log excerpt and ask for a fix.
- Optional local check on this computer: clone, `npm ci`, `npx expo-doctor`, `npm test`.
- Run `npx expo install --check` for version mismatches.

## 5. Hand off
Tell the owner: repo link, PR link, what's in it, what's next. Next is usually: the owner runs `eas init` linking to their Expo account (or adds an EXPO_TOKEN to bot secrets), then `ios-android-builds` for a first development build, then `build-feature-with-cloud-agent` for each MVP screen.

skills.name: build-feature-with-cloud-agent
skills.description: Use when the owner asks for a new feature, screen, bug fix, or refactor in the app code. All code changes go through a cloud agent and a reviewed PR.
skills.content:
---
name: build-feature-with-cloud-agent
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks for a new feature, screen, bug fix, or refactor in the
  app code. All code changes go through a cloud agent and a reviewed PR.
---
# Build a feature with a cloud agent

## 1. Shape the work (before launching)
- Restate the feature in 1-2 lines and confirm only if it is ambiguous.
- Read the repo context you need: docs/SPEC.md, route tree, related files, open PRs touching the same area (avoid conflicts).
- Split anything bigger than ~1 day of work into independent PR-sized tasks. Launch independent ones in parallel; chain dependent ones.
- Decide if it needs native changes (new native module, permission, config plugin, app.config change). If yes, it will need a new binary, not just an OTA update (see `release-train`).

## 2. Prompt template
```
Goal: <one sentence user-facing outcome>
Context: Expo SDK <n>, expo-router, TypeScript. Relevant files: <paths>. Conventions: <state lib, styling, API client>.
Build:
- <screen/route path> with <components>, loading/empty/error states
- Data: <entities, API calls, storage>
- Platform notes: <iOS/Android differences, permissions + purpose strings in app.config>
- Accessibility: labels on interactive elements, dynamic type does not break layout
Tests: unit tests for logic, RNTL test for the screen happy path + one error path.
Acceptance criteria:
1. <observable behavior>
2. <observable behavior>
3. lint, typecheck, tests pass in CI
Out of scope: <list>. Do not bump the Expo SDK, change bundle IDs, or touch eas.json/credentials unless asked.
Open a PR titled "<type>: <summary>" with a description listing changes and how to test.
```

## 3. Review the PR (never skip)
Check, in order: acceptance criteria met; diff scoped to the task; no secrets, no hardcoded API keys, no debug logs; permissions have honest purpose strings; no new heavy dependency without reason (`npx expo install` versions); tests meaningful; CI green.
If anything fails, reply to the same cloud agent with a numbered list of fixes and the failing log lines. Repeat until clean. Do not hand-edit code yourself.

## 4. Get a preview in the owner's hands
Pick the lightest option that works:
- JS-only change and a preview/development build already installed: publish to a branch with `eas update --branch pr-<n> --message "<summary>"` and share the update link/QR from the EAS dashboard.
- Native change, or no build installed yet: `eas build --profile preview` (or development) via `ios-android-builds`, share the install link.
- Expo Go works only for projects without custom native code and its store version has lagged new SDKs in 2026; prefer development builds.
EAS commands need the owner's Expo login or an EXPO_TOKEN in bot secrets. Builds can consume paid EAS quota on paid plans; mention it if the owner is on a metered plan.

## 5. Report to the owner
Short message: what changed (bullets), PR link, preview link/QR, what to test (2-4 steps), known limits. Ask for "merge?" Merge only on explicit yes (or if the owner has given standing permission for this repo, saved in memory).
After merge, note the change for the changelog in `release-train`.

skills.name: ios-android-builds
skills.description: Use when the owner needs an installable build (dev, internal test, TestFlight, Play testing, or store-ready), or when an EAS build fails.
skills.content:
---
name: ios-android-builds
description: >-
  Use when the owner needs an installable build (dev, internal test, TestFlight,
  Play testing, or store-ready), or when an EAS build fails.
---
# iOS and Android builds (EAS)

This computer is Linux, so iOS builds always run in the cloud: EAS Build (default), Xcode Cloud or a self-hosted Mac runner (native projects). Android can also build in EAS.

## Setup (once)
- Install CLI on this computer: `npm i -g eas-cli`, check `eas --version`.
- Auth: the owner either signs in themselves (`eas login` in a terminal they control) or creates an Expo access token (robot user preferred) and stores it as EXPO_TOKEN in bot secrets. Never ask for passwords in chat.
- `eas init` links the project. Confirm `eas.json` has profiles:
  - development: developmentClient true, distribution internal
  - preview: distribution internal, channel "preview"
  - production: autoIncrement true, channel "production"
  - `cli.appVersionSource: "remote"` so EAS manages buildNumber/versionCode. You still bump the user-facing `version` per release (see `release-train`).
- Credentials: let EAS manage them. iOS: first build needs an interactive Apple sign-in by the owner (or an App Store Connect API key the owner uploads at expo.dev > project > credentials). Android: EAS generates the upload keystore; Play App Signing holds the app signing key. Remind the owner to keep the keystore backed up in EAS.

## Commands
- Dev client: `eas build -p ios --profile development` (register devices with `eas device:create` first for internal iOS installs), `-p android` for Android.
- Internal test: `eas build -p all --profile preview`, share install links.
- Store builds: `eas build -p all --profile production` (iOS .ipa, Android .aab). Store submissions only via `app-store-submission`.
- Add `--non-interactive --no-wait` from this computer; track with `eas build:list --limit 5 --json` and `eas build:view <id>`.

## Requirements to check at runtime (2026 reference values)
- Apple: since Apr 28 2026 uploads must be built with Xcode 26+ and the iOS 26 SDK. Check https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ for the next bump (Apple usually raises it each spring).
- EAS image: default `auto` picks the image for your SDK (SDK 57 maps to an Xcode 26.x image). Check https://docs.expo.dev/build-reference/infrastructure/ before pinning.
- Google Play: since Aug 31 2026 new apps and updates must target Android 16 (API 36); extension forms ran to Nov 1 2026. Check https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk. Current Expo SDKs set this; verify `targetSdkVersion` in the build log.

## Testing tracks
- iOS: TestFlight internal testers (team members, no review) and external testers (needs Beta App Review). `npx testflight` is a shortcut that builds and submits to TestFlight; only run with owner confirmation.
- Android: internal testing (up to 100 testers, fast), closed testing (required 12 testers x 14 days for new personal accounts), open testing.

## Troubleshooting (read the failing phase in the build log first)
- Install dependencies fails: lockfile mismatch, run `npx expo install --check`; private packages need NPM_TOKEN as an EAS env var.
- Pod install / CocoaPods errors: version conflicts after adding a native lib; ensure versions from `npx expo install`, clear cache with `--clear-cache`.
- Provisioning profile / capability errors: a new entitlement (push, Sign in with Apple, associated domains) was added; run `eas credentials` (owner) to regenerate the profile.
- Gradle OOM or duplicate class: bump resource class to large, dedupe dependencies.
- "Missing compliance" in TestFlight: set `ios.config.usesNonExemptEncryption: false` if the app only uses standard HTTPS/OS encryption (owner confirms).
- Build works, app crashes on launch: check Sentry, missing EXPO_PUBLIC_ env in that profile, or a native module not in the build (needs rebuild, not OTA).
Fix code issues via a cloud agent (`build-feature-with-cloud-agent`), then rebuild.

skills.name: store-listing-and-aso
skills.description: Use when preparing or improving App Store / Google Play listing text, keywords, screenshots, icon, or feature graphic.
skills.content:
---
name: store-listing-and-aso
description: >-
  Use when preparing or improving App Store / Google Play listing text,
  keywords, screenshots, icon, or feature graphic.
---
# Store listing and ASO

Draft everything, the owner approves everything. Store text is public; nothing goes live without a yes.

## Research (10 minutes)
- Search both stores for the app's top 5 search terms. Note competitor names, subtitles, first screenshot message, and complaint themes in their low-star reviews.
- Pick 1 primary keyword and 3-5 secondary ones. Never claim "#1", "best", awards, or user counts you can't prove (Play metadata policy bans rank/price/promo claims in title, icon, and graphics).

## Text fields (limits change rarely, but recheck in the consoles)
| Field | App Store | Google Play |
|---|---|---|
| Name/title | 30 chars | 30 chars |
| Subtitle / short description | 30 chars | 80 chars |
| Keywords | 100 chars, comma-separated, no spaces, don't repeat words from name | none (full description is indexed) |
| Promotional text | 170 chars, editable without review | n/a |
| Description | up to 4000 chars (not indexed for search) | up to 4000 chars (indexed, use keywords naturally) |
| What's New | per version | release notes, 500 chars per language |
Write: benefit-first first line, 3-5 short feature bullets, social proof only if real, clear subscription terms if any.

## Visual assets (verified Oct 2026; recheck the help pages)
- iOS screenshots: 1-10 per size, JPEG/PNG. Required iPhone set 6.9" (1320x2868, 1290x2796 or 1260x2736 portrait), or 6.5" if no 6.9". iPad 13" (2064x2752 or 2048x2732) required only if the app runs on iPad, so set `ios.supportsTablet: false` for phone-only apps. Source: developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-information/screenshot-specifications/
- iOS icon: 1024x1024 PNG, no transparency, set via app.config `icon`.
- Play screenshots: 2-8 per device type, JPEG or 24-bit PNG (no alpha), sides 320-3840 px, long side at most 2x short side; give at least 4 phone screenshots at 1080 px+ (e.g. 1080x1920) to be eligible for recommendation surfaces.
- Play icon: 512x512 32-bit PNG, max 1024 KB, no pre-rounded corners. Feature graphic: 1024x500 JPEG or 24-bit PNG, no alpha, required.
Source: support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9866151

## Screenshot plan
1. First 2-3 frames carry the message: one benefit headline (3-6 words) over a real app screen.
2. Order: core loop, key differentiator, proof (progress/results), customization, paywall value (if any).
3. Capture real screens: ask a cloud agent to add a Maestro flow or a screenshot script that runs on EAS (iOS simulator + Android emulator), or the owner captures on device. Then frame them: generate backgrounds with image generation, composite with a script (ImageMagick/Pillow) at exact pixel sizes, strip alpha for Play.
4. Never show features that don't exist (App Review 2.3 accurate metadata).

## Deliver
Write `store/listing.md` (both stores, each locale) and `store/screenshots/<platform>/<size>/` in the repo via a cloud agent PR, or as files on this computer. Show the owner a side-by-side preview and a checklist of what's missing. For updates, rewrite only what changed and propose one A/B idea (Play store listing experiments, App Store product page optimization).

skills.name: app-store-submission
skills.description: Use when a build is ready to go to App Store review or Google Play production/testing tracks, or when a store rejects the app.
skills.content:
---
name: app-store-submission
description: >-
  Use when a build is ready to go to App Store review or Google Play
  production/testing tracks, or when a store rejects the app.
---
# App store submission

HARD RULE: never run `eas submit`, press submit in a console, or release a build without the owner's explicit "yes, submit <version> to <store>" in this conversation. Show the checklist result first.

## Pre-submission checklist (both stores; mark each pass/fail/NA)
- Build: production profile, correct bundle ID/package, version bumped, Sentry release set, no dev menus or test endpoints.
- Platform minimums met (check at runtime): iOS built with Xcode 26+/iOS 26 SDK (since Apr 28 2026); Android targets API 36 (since Aug 31 2026); Play Billing Library 8+ if selling in-app on Android.
- Privacy policy URL live, also linked inside the app (App Review 5.1.1(i)).
- Account deletion if accounts exist: in-app path (5.1.1(v)) AND, for Play, a public web URL where users can request deletion, entered in Data safety.
- iOS privacy: App Privacy "nutrition label" answers match real data collection, including SDKs (Sentry, RevenueCat, analytics). Privacy manifest: Expo apps declare required-reason APIs under `ios.privacyManifests` in app config; third-party SDKs ship their own.
- Play Data safety form completed and consistent with the policy.
- Permission purpose strings specific and honest; only request permissions the app uses, at the moment it needs them.
- Age rating: Apple's updated questionnaire (13+/16+/18+ tiers; social media capability questions required for submissions since Sep 2026). Play content rating (IARC) questionnaire.
- Export compliance answered (`usesNonExemptEncryption`).
- Review notes: what the app does, how to reach key features, demo account credentials created by the owner (never real user data), notes on hardware/region needs.
- Sign in with Apple offered if other third-party logins are used (4.8). Restore Purchases present if selling subscriptions.
- Store listing complete (`store-listing-and-aso`), EU trader status set in App Store Connect if distributing in the EU.
- Google Play new personal account (created after Nov 13 2023): closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for the last 14 continuous days, then apply for production access (review usually up to ~7 days). Plan this weeks ahead.
- First Android upload: Google requires the first AAB to be uploaded manually in Play Console before API uploads (`eas submit`) work. The owner does it.

## Submit (after explicit yes)
- iOS: `eas submit -p ios --latest` (uses the App Store Connect API key the owner stored in EAS). Then the owner (or you, if asked) adds the build to the version and submits for review in App Store Connect. Suggest phased release (see `release-train`).
- Android: `eas submit -p android --latest` with track internal/closed/production as agreed (service account key stored in EAS by the owner). Suggest staged rollout.
- Record version, build numbers, date, and track in memory for `weekly-app-health`.

## Rejection playbook
Read the full rejection message, quote it to the owner, map it, fix via `build-feature-with-cloud-agent`, reply in Resolution Center (draft for owner approval).
- 2.1 App Completeness: crash, broken link, placeholder content, or reviewer couldn't log in. Fix the bug, verify on device, provide a working demo account and clear steps.
- 2.3 Accurate Metadata: screenshots/description show missing features. Regenerate assets from the real app.
- 4.2 Minimum Functionality: looks like a repackaged website or too thin. Add native value (offline, notifications, device features, real utility) and explain it in notes.
- 4.3 Spam: duplicate of your other apps or a common template. Consolidate apps, differentiate meaningfully; do not resubmit unchanged.
- 5.1.1 Data Collection: vague purpose strings, forced login for non-account features, missing deletion, policy gaps. Rewrite strings, allow guest use where possible, add deletion.
- 3.1.1 In-App Purchase: digital content unlocked outside IAP. Move to IAP (`monetization-setup`). On the US storefront, links to external purchase are allowed since May 2025; elsewhere they need a regional entitlement. Check current guideline text.
- 4.8 Login Services: add Sign in with Apple or equivalent.
- Play policy rejections: read the policy cited in the email; common ones are Data safety mismatch, missing deletion URL, permissions (background location, SMS, all-files access) needing a declaration.
If the owner believes the rejection is wrong, draft a polite, factual reply or an App Review appeal for them to send.

skills.name: monetization-setup
skills.description: Use when adding a paywall, subscriptions, one-time purchases, or changing prices in the app.
skills.content:
---
name: monetization-setup
description: >-
  Use when adding a paywall, subscriptions, one-time purchases, or changing
  prices in the app.
---
# Monetization setup

Default: RevenueCat (one SDK for both stores, server-side receipt validation, entitlements, paywall UI). Alternatives: StoreKit 2 + Play Billing directly (native apps or no third party wanted), or `expo-iap`-style libraries. Never invent revenue or conversion numbers; if asked, point to public benchmark reports with links and say they vary widely.

## Prerequisites the owner must do (they sign in, not you)
- Apple: sign the Paid Apps Agreement, add tax and banking in App Store Connect > Business. Consider the App Store Small Business Program (check current terms).
- Google: set up a payments profile in Play Console; an app with the BILLING permission must have been uploaded to a track before products can be created.
- RevenueCat: create a project, add the iOS app (App Store Connect API key / in-app purchase key) and Android app (service account JSON) in its dashboard. Keys go into RevenueCat, not chat.

## Products
1. Decide the model with the owner: subscription (monthly + annual is a common start), one-time unlock, or consumables. One entitlement (e.g. `pro`) covering everything paid keeps it simple.
2. Product IDs identical across stores where possible, e.g. `app_pro_monthly`, `app_pro_annual`.
3. App Store Connect: create a subscription group, add products, prices, localized names, review screenshot. Play Console: create subscriptions with base plans (and offers for free trials/intro prices).
4. In RevenueCat: import products, attach to entitlement, create an Offering (default) with packages.
Pricing guidance: look up 3-5 competitor prices on both stores (cite), pick tiers per region with the stores' price templates, offer annual at a visible discount vs monthly. The owner decides final prices.

## Code (cloud agent prompt essentials)
- `npx expo install react-native-purchases react-native-purchases-ui`; requires a development build (Expo Go only mocks purchases).
- Configure once at app start with platform-specific public SDK keys from EXPO_PUBLIC_ env vars; set the user ID after login (`Purchases.logIn`).
- Gate features on `customerInfo.entitlements.active.pro`, listen for updates.
- Paywall: RevenueCat Paywalls (`RevenueCatUI.presentPaywallIfNeeded`) or a custom screen. Must show price, billing period, trial terms, Restore Purchases button, links to Terms of Use (EULA) and Privacy Policy (Apple 3.1.2).
- Android: confirm the RevenueCat SDK version uses Play Billing Library 8+ (required for new apps and updates since Aug 31 2026).
- Tests for gating logic with a mocked SDK.

## Sandbox testing
- iOS: Sandbox Apple Account (App Store Connect > Users and Access > Sandbox), test on a TestFlight or development build; renewals are accelerated.
- Android: add license testers in Play Console; install from an internal testing track.
- Test: purchase, cancel, restore on reinstall, upgrade monthly to annual, expired state, offline launch. Check events in the RevenueCat dashboard.

## Before release
Products in "Ready to Submit" (Apple: first subscription must be submitted with an app version). Update App Privacy / Data safety for purchase history. Hand off to `app-store-submission`.

skills.name: release-train
skills.description: Use when planning or shipping a release: versioning, changelog, OTA update vs new binary, phased/staged rollout, or rollback.
skills.content:
---
name: release-train
description: >-
  Use when planning or shipping a release: versioning, changelog, OTA update vs
  new binary, phased/staged rollout, or rollback.
---
# Release train

## Versioning
- User-facing `version` uses semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: PATCH = fixes, MINOR = features, MAJOR = big redesign or breaking account/data change.
- Build numbers (iOS buildNumber, Android versionCode) are managed remotely by EAS (`appVersionSource: remote`, `autoIncrement`). Never reuse one.
- Runtime version (`policy: "fingerprint"`) decides which OTA updates a binary can take.

## OTA update or new binary?
OTA (`eas update`) is fine when ALL are true: only JS/TS and assets changed; no new native module or config plugin; no change to app.config native fields (permissions, icon, splash, scheme, entitlements); Expo SDK unchanged; the fingerprint/runtime version is unchanged (`npx expo-fingerprint` or check `eas update` output).
New binary otherwise. Also ship a binary for anything that changes the app's primary purpose or adds major features: Apple allows interpreted-code updates only when they don't change the app's purpose or bypass review. Keep OTAs to fixes and small improvements.

## Release steps
1. Freeze: list merged PRs since the last tag (`git log <lastTag>..main --merges` or the GitHub connector). Group into Features / Fixes / Internal.
2. Changelog: write CHANGELOG.md entry plus user-facing "What's New" (plain words, 3-5 bullets, no internal jargon). Owner approves the user-facing text.
3. Bump version via a small cloud agent PR (app.config version + CHANGELOG), merge on approval, tag `vX.Y.Z`.
4. Binary path: `ios-android-builds` production build, then `app-store-submission` (explicit yes required). OTA path: `eas update --channel production --message "vX.Y.Z: <summary>"` only after the owner says go.

## Rollout
- iOS phased release: 7-day automatic ramp for auto-updating users (owner enables at release; can pause or release to all).
- Google Play staged rollout: start low (e.g. 5-10%), raise after a day or two of clean crash and ANR data; halt if bad.
- EAS Update: `eas update --rollout-percentage=10`, raise with `eas update:edit`, end at 100 or revert with `eas update:revert-update-rollout`. Branch-based: `eas channel:rollout`.
Watch Sentry/Crashlytics crash-free rate and new issues between steps (`crash-and-review-triage`).

## Rollback
- OTA: `eas update:rollback` (or republish the previous update / revert the rollout). Fastest fix path for JS bugs.
- Binary: stores have no true rollback. iOS: pause phased release, ship a fix build (request expedited review for critical bugs). Play: halt staged rollout, then ship a higher versionCode with the fix.
- Always write a 3-line incident note to memory: what broke, impact, fix.

## After release
Record version, date, channels, rollout state in memory. Tell the owner: shipped what, to whom, what you're watching, when you'll check back.

skills.description: Use when the owner asks about crashes, errors, bad ratings, or user reviews, or after a release to check its health.

---
name: crash-and-review-triage
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks about crashes, errors, bad ratings, or user reviews,
  or after a release to check its health.
---
# Crash and review triage

## 1. Pull data (last 7 days unless asked otherwise)
Crashes, in order of preference:
- Sentry connector: unresolved issues for the production environment, sorted by users affected; release health (crash-free sessions/users) per release.
- Firebase connector (Crashlytics): top issues by affected users, new and regressed issues, per version.
- Neither connected: ask the owner once to connect Sentry or Firebase from the connectors page. Meanwhile use what exists (Play Console Android vitals, App Store Connect crashes) via exports the owner shares.
Reviews:
- App Store: App Store Connect API customer reviews (needs an API key the owner stores in bot secrets), or the public store page/RSS for read-only text.
- Google Play: Play Developer API reviews (needs a service account; only returns reviews created or edited in the last 7 days, so run at least weekly), or owner export.
Never scrape behind a login with the owner's session.

## 2. Cluster and rank
- Crashes: group by root cause, not just stack top frame (same exception + same app frame = one cluster). Rank by users affected x trend (new or growing first), then by whether it hits a core flow (launch, login, purchase).
- Reviews: tag each with theme (bug, performance, UX, missing feature, pricing, praise), platform, version, rating. Count per theme. Link review clusters to crash clusters when they match (same version, same screen).
- Mark regressions: issues first seen in the latest release.

## 3. Act
For each top cluster (max 5), produce: title, users affected, versions, evidence (stack frame, review quotes), likely cause, proposed fix, effort guess (S/M/L).
- Open an issue in the tracker the owner uses (GitHub Issues by default, Linear if connected) only if the owner has allowed issue creation; otherwise list drafts and ask "open these?". Creating tickets is a visible action.
- For S-sized, high-impact fixes, offer to launch a cloud agent right away via `build-feature-with-cloud-agent`, with the stack trace, breadcrumbs, and a regression test requirement in the prompt.
- If a JS-only fix, recommend an OTA update with a rollout (`release-train`).

## 4. Review replies (draft only)
Draft replies for 1-2 star reviews and any review mentioning a fixed bug. Rules: thank, be specific, no defensiveness, no personal data, mention the fix version only if it's live, under ~350 chars (Play limit is 350 chars). Present drafts in a numbered list; post only the ones the owner approves, via the connector/API or the owner pastes them.

## 5. Report format
```
Crash-free users: <x>% (prev <y>%) | Ratings: iOS <a> (n), Android <b> (n)
Top issues:
1. <title> - <users> users, v<ver>, <new/regressed> -> <action>
Review themes: <theme> (<count>), ...
Drafted: <n> replies (awaiting approval) | Proposed fixes: <n> (awaiting go)
```
Use real numbers only; if a source is missing, say "not connected".

skills.description: Use when the weekly-app-health routine fires, or the owner asks "how's the app doing" / "anything I need to do".
skills.content:
---
name: weekly-app-health
description: >-
  Use when the weekly-app-health routine fires, or the owner asks "how's the app
  doing" / "anything I need to do".
---
# Weekly app health digest

Goal: one short message the owner can read in a minute, ending with the top 3 actions. Silence on things that are fine.

## Gather (skip sources that aren't connected; say so once at the bottom)
1. Stability: run the data pull from `crash-and-review-triage` (7 days). Crash-free users/sessions vs last week, new and regressed issues.
2. Ratings and reviews: average and count per store this week, new 1-2 star themes.
3. Code: open PRs and their age, cloud agent PRs waiting on review, CI status of the default branch, Dependabot/security alerts if the GitHub connector shows them.
4. Builds and store status: latest EAS builds (`eas build:list --limit 5 --json`), App Store review state and Play track/rollout state if accessible, any phased/staged/OTA rollout in progress and its percentage.
5. Deadlines and expiries (check live sources each run, compare with memory):
   - Google Play target API: since Aug 31 2026 new apps/updates must target API 36; extension forms ran to Nov 1 2026. The requirement rises yearly (usually Aug 31). Source: developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk
   - Apple minimum SDK: Xcode 26 / iOS 26 SDK since Apr 28 2026; watch developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ for the next one.
   - Play Billing Library: 8+ required for new apps/updates since Aug 31 2026 (if selling on Android).
   - Expo SDK: each SDK gets roughly a year of support; flag when the app is 2+ SDKs behind latest stable (expo.dev/changelog).
   - Apple distribution certificate and provisioning profile expiry (`eas credentials` shows dates), push key validity, Apple Developer membership renewal date (ask the owner once, store in memory).
   - Play closed-test countdown (12 testers x 14 days) if still pending production access.
   - Policy emails/notices the owner forwards or that appear in connected mail.
6. Last week's actions: were they done? Carry over anything open.

## Write the digest
```
App health, week of <date>
Stability: crash-free users <x>% (<+/-> vs last week). <n> new issues.
Ratings: iOS <a> (<n> new), Android <b> (<n> new). Themes: <top 2>.
Code: <n> PRs open (<n> waiting on you), main CI <green/red>.
Releases: <version + rollout state, or "none in flight">.
Deadlines: <only items due within 60 days, with dates>.
Top 3 actions:
1. <action> - <why, one line> - <who: me after your OK / you>
2. ...
3. ...
Not connected: <list, if any>
```
Rules: real numbers only, no padding, max ~15 lines. Prefer actions that protect users (crash fixes, deadline compliance) over nice-to-haves. Offer to start action 1 right away (e.g. launch a fix agent) but do not start anything visible or costly without a yes.

## Save
Append a 2-line summary to memory (date, crash-free, rating, actions) so next week can show trends and follow-ups.
